## A — Sharing the Road
Authority: the Maine Bureau of Motor Vehicles presents this manual as preparation for safe vehicle operation and obtaining a driver license. [A06]
Source title: Maine Driver’s License Manual, issued under the Secretary of State. [A01]
Pinned edition: the frontmatter revision marker is Rev 4/24. [A02]
Selected path: first-time applicants studying the standard Class C license material; commercial endorsements are excluded. [A08]
Official question count remains unknown (verify ME-SEC10-COUNT); official passing standard remains unknown (verify ME-SEC10-PASS); official time limit remains unknown (verify ME-SEC10-TIME).
This dossier’s subject is Sharing the Road; the source map controls coverage rather than an invented official exam weight.
Any quiz mastery target belongs to the accepted LearningLoop as product policy; it is not an official passing score.
The current issuer observation confirms this pinned document; an unknown legal effective date is retained in the registrar’s accepted disposition.

sections.heading: B — Sharing the Road
sections.markdown:
## B — Sharing the Road
Audience: English-language first-time standard-license applicants using the Sharing the Road section.
Level: beginner study of the selected handbook material, followed by recall and application practice.
Prerequisite policy: understand the cited terminology before comparing exceptions; this is a teaching order, not an extra licensing eligibility requirement.
Coverage basis: the physical source range and the fact roster define this topic; no official topic percentage was supplied.

sections.markdown:
## C — Sharing the Road

FACT_ID: sec10-F01 | anchor: A101
Share the roadway courteously and communicate your position and intended movement to other users. [A101]

FACT_ID: sec10-F02 | anchor: A101
Yield to people crossing in a marked crosswalk, including when traffic-control equipment is not operating. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec10-F03 | anchor: A101
The manual’s safety guidance also directs yielding to pedestrians outside crosswalks and when your traffic signal is green. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec10-F04 | anchor: A101
Stop completely for a pedestrian crossing with a guide dog or white cane. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec10-F05 | anchor: A101
Do not pass a vehicle that has stopped or is slowing to yield to someone in a crosswalk. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec10-F06 | anchor: A101
Yield to pedestrians when making a permitted turn on red. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec10-F07 | anchor: A101
Watch for people beside parked or stopped vehicles, and check behind before backing in parking lots. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec10-F08 | anchor: A101
Reduce speed near homes and playgrounds and be ready for children to emerge between parked cars. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec10-F09 | anchor: A101
At a school crossing, stop and yield when directed by the crossing guard. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec10-F10 | anchor: A101
Follow the reduced school-zone speed when warning lights flash or children are present outside. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec10-F11 | anchor: A101
Before crossing a sidewalk, yield to pedestrians and cyclists using it. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec10-F12 | anchor: A101
Exercise care to avoid striking pedestrians or cyclists regardless of other traffic rules. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec10-F13 | anchor: A101
A bicycle is a vehicle, and its rider shares vehicle drivers’ road rights and responsibilities. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec10-F14 | anchor: A102

Source: [A102 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec10-F15 | anchor: A102

Source: [A102 -> pdf-0102]

Source: [A102 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec10-F18 | anchor: A102

Source: [A102 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec10-F19 | anchor: A102
Slow for an approaching or overtaken cyclist and let the rider clear an intersection before you turn. [A102]
Source: [A102 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec10-F20 | anchor: A102
Cyclists generally ride as far right as practical, but may choose another position when staying right is unsafe. [A102]
Source: [A102 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec10-F21 | anchor: A102
On a lane too narrow for safe side-by-side travel, a cyclist may ride near its center. [A102]
Source: [A102 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec10-F22 | anchor: A102
Check carefully for cyclists before a turn or opening a vehicle door. [A102]
Source: [A102 -> pdf-0102]

Give cyclists room to avoid potholes, debris and drain grates. [A102]

Although cyclists should travel with traffic, search for riders approaching from any direction. [A103]
Source: [A103 -> pdf-0103]

Source: [A103 -> pdf-0103]

Source: [A104 -> pdf-0104]

Source: [A104 -> pdf-0104]

Source: [A104 -> pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec10-F41 | anchor: A104

Source: [A104 -> pdf-0104]

Source: [A104 -> pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec10-F43 | anchor: A104

Source: [A104 -> pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec10-F44 | anchor: A104

Source: [A104 -> pdf-0104]

Source: [A104 -> pdf-0104]

Source: [A104 -> pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec10-F47 | anchor: A104

Source: [A104 -> pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec10-F48 | anchor: A104
For a vehicle-style left turn on a bicycle, check behind, signal and move left only when clear. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec10-F49 | anchor: A104

Source: [A104 -> pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec10-F50 | anchor: A104
The manual’s bicycle night equipment includes a white front lamp visible at least 200 feet ahead and a red or amber rear lamp or reflector visible at least 200 feet behind. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec10-F51 | anchor: A104
Reflective bicycle pedals are recommended unless reflective material is worn on the feet or ankles. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec10-F52 | anchor: A104
Cyclists should allow extra stopping room in rain and carry suitable clothing and water. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec10-F53 | anchor: A105
Motorcyclists share other drivers’ road rights and responsibilities; motorcycle licensing uses a separate manual. [A105]
Source: [A105 -> pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec10-F54 | anchor: A105

Source: [A105 -> pdf-0105]

Mnemonic: look, yield, leave room, communicate.
Glossary: a bicycle is a vehicle with road rights and duties. [A101]
Dynamic facts: legal coverage, equipment standards and undated traffic statistics remain review debt.

sections.heading: C2 — Sharing the Road
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Sharing the Road

FACT_ID: sec10-R01 | anchor: A105
Check mirrors and blind spots carefully for small, less visible motorcycles. [A105]
Source: [A105 -> pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec10-R02 | anchor: A105
Look ahead and to the sides before a left turn and wait for an oncoming motorcycle to pass. [A105]
Source: [A105 -> pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec10-R03 | anchor: A105
A flashing motorcycle turn signal may have been left on because it does not always cancel automatically. [A105]
Source: [A105 -> pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec10-R04 | anchor: A105
Leave at least a 4-second following gap behind a motorcycle and increase it when the road is wet. [A105]
Source: [A105 -> pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec10-R05 | anchor: A105
Expect a rider to change speed or lane position to avoid potholes, loose material, slick spots, seams or railway crossings. [A105]
Source: [A105 -> pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec10-R06 | anchor: A106
Large vehicles have extensive blind spots despite their mirrors, so avoid remaining in those areas. [A106]
Source: [A106 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec10-R07 | anchor: A106
Never pass behind a reversing bus or truck. [A106]
Source: [A106 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec10-R08 | anchor: A106
If a large vehicle’s mirrors are not visible to you, its driver probably cannot see you. [A106]
Source: [A106 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec10-R09 | anchor: A106
Allow buses and trucks extra room for acceleration, braking and turning. [A106]
Source: [A106 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec10-R10 | anchor: A106
A large vehicle can lose speed sharply uphill or gain it quickly downhill, so avoid taking away its operating space. [A106]
Source: [A106 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec10-R11 | anchor: A106
When a large vehicle follows you, leave ample room ahead so both drivers have time to respond. [A106]
Source: [A106 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec10-R12 | anchor: A106
Do not pull or pass in front of a large vehicle that is already slowing or stopping. [A106]
Source: [A106 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec10-R13 | anchor: A106
A truck or bus may swing left before a right turn; watch its position and signals and stay clear of the turn path. [A106]
Source: [A106 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec10-R14 | anchor: A107
No-Zones are large-vehicle blind areas at the front, rear and sides. [A107]
Source: [A107 -> pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec10-R15 | anchor: A107
The manual identifies a truck’s largest side blind area on its right, extending rearward from the cab. [A107]
Source: [A107 -> pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec10-R16 | anchor: A107
Avoid lingering beside a large vehicle because a sudden lane change or swerve can cause a collision. [A107]
Source: [A107 -> pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec10-R17 | anchor: A107
After passing a large vehicle, wait until its whole front is visible in your rearview mirror before returning to its lane. [A107]
Source: [A107 -> pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec10-R18 | anchor: A107
Do not tailgate a truck to draft in its wake; close following also blocks your view ahead. [A107]
Source: [A107 -> pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec10-R19 | anchor: A107
When stopped behind a large vehicle uphill, leave room for possible rollback as it starts. [A107]
Source: [A107 -> pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec10-R20 | anchor: A108
Wait until a large vehicle completes its turn before making a turn into its path. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec10-R21 | anchor: A108
To reduce wind effects from an oncoming truck, use the rightmost portion of your own lane. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec10-R22 | anchor: A108
If uncertain about an oncoming truck’s speed, wait for it to pass before turning left. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec10-R23 | anchor: A108
Stop behind intersection stop lines so large vehicles have turning clearance. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec10-R24 | anchor: A108
Do not cut ahead of a truck or race it into a construction section that narrows to one lane. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec10-R25 | anchor: A108
Give large vehicles additional space on every side in bad weather or limited visibility. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec10-R26 | anchor: A108
On slick roads, avoid maneuvers that force a bus or truck to brake unnecessarily. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec10-R27 | anchor: A108
Following a large vehicle too closely both hides you from its driver and limits your view of the road. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec10-R28 | anchor: A109
Dim headlights when following a large vehicle at night to avoid glare in its mirrors. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec10-R29 | anchor: A109
Before passing a large vehicle, inspect ahead, behind and the side you intend to move toward. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec10-R30 | anchor: A109
Pass a large vehicle only in a legal passing area and only when the maneuver can be completed without speeding. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec10-R31 | anchor: A109
Check over your shoulder before returning to the right lane after passing a bus or truck. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec10-R32 | anchor: A109
If a large vehicle passes you, stay to the right within your lane until it clears and maintain speed or ease off slightly. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec10-R33 | anchor: A109
On wet roads, start the wipers before a passing large vehicle throws spray across your view. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec10-R34 | anchor: A109
Yield to an emergency vehicle using flashing lights and a siren by pulling to the road edge and stopping. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec10-R35 | anchor: A109
Clear an intersection before pulling aside for an emergency vehicle; do not block the intersection. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec10-R36 | anchor: A109
Do not follow a fire truck responding to an alarm within 500 feet. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec10-R37 | anchor: A110
For a police stop, pull to a safe place on the right and remain inside unless asked to leave the vehicle. [A110] [A109]
Source: [A110 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec10-R38 | anchor: A110
During a police stop, shut off the engine, switch on hazard flashers and open the window for communication. [A110] [A109]
Source: [A110 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec10-R39 | anchor: A110
At a night police stop, switch on the interior light so the officer can see inside. [A110] [A109]
Source: [A110 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec10-R40 | anchor: A110
Stay calm and keep seat belts fastened during a traffic stop, including those of passengers. [A110] [A109]
Source: [A110 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec10-R41 | anchor: A110
Keep hands on the steering wheel during a traffic stop. [A110] [A109]
Source: [A110 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec10-R42 | anchor: A110
If an officer requests license, insurance or registration, explain where it is and reach slowly while keeping one hand on the wheel. [A110] [A109]
Source: [A110 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec10-R43 | anchor: A110
Do not try to flee a traffic stop. [A110] [A109]
Source: [A110 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec10-R44 | anchor: A110
For an emergency vehicle stopped at the roadside, slow and yield; change into the next lane when possible and safe. [A110]
Source: [A110 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec10-R45 | anchor: A110
If moving over is unsafe, slow down and pass the stopped emergency vehicle cautiously. [A110]
Source: [A110 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec10-R46 | anchor: A110
The rear orange-and-red reflective or fluorescent triangle identifies a vehicle traveling below 25 mph. [A110]
Source: [A110 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec10-R47 | anchor: A110
Approach a slow-moving vehicle cautiously and pass only after confirming it is safe. [A110]
Source: [A110 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec10-R48 | anchor: A111
Watch for farm equipment crossing rural roads or using highways, and pass carefully because its operator may not see or hear you. [A111]
Source: [A111 -> pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec10-R49 | anchor: A111
Slow and pass animals or animal-drawn vehicles cautiously because a startled animal may rear, swerve or stop. [A111]
Source: [A111 -> pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec10-R50 | anchor: A111
Horse riders and horse-drawn vehicles share the road and follow vehicle traffic rules. [A111]
Source: [A111 -> pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec10-R51 | anchor: A111
Avoid using the horn or revving the engine near an animal, and never deliberately frighten an animal ridden, driven or led near a public way. [A111]
Source: [A111 -> pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec10-R52 | anchor: A111
Watch for animal-drawn traffic turning left into a field or driveway and heed signs warning of that traffic. [A111]
Source: [A111 -> pdf-0111]

sections.heading: D — Sharing the Road
sections.markdown:
## D — Sharing the Road
Accuracy scope: Sharing the Road facts use the pinned official PDF with a registered primary page and any explicitly declared supporting pages; original phrasing preserves actor qualifications, exceptions and modal verbs.
The bicycle-signal photographs, truck blind-area diagrams and rear slow-moving triangle were actually inspected. No handedness, diagram scale, measured clearance or palm orientation is inferred from a front/back-ambiguous photograph. [A103] [A107] [A110]
Undated bicycle totals, motorcycle fleet/fatality percentages, annual truck-crash totals and cyclist speed illustrations are not taught as current measured facts. [A101] [A102] [A105]
The universal comparison of car-versus-bicycle stopping performance, fixed truck stopping illustration, rear-blind-area estimate and drafting physics assertion need assumptions before quantitative or universal learner use. [A102] [A107]
Helmet product approvals, fixed replacement intervals, heat effects and injury-reduction claims need current product/safety evidence; the published age rule remains a pinned legal statement pending currentness review. [A104]
Pedestrian yielding is safety guidance, not universal fault allocation; midblock marked/unmarked wording is unclear. Categorical answering of police questions is not authored as a waiver of legal rights. [A101] [A110]
Move-over coverage is limited to the stopped emergency vehicles actually named here; no unverified extension to tow, utility or other vehicle classes is invented. [A110]
Confidence process: every drafted fact received a same-model source-context check before submission; independent coverage and hallucination QA remain pending.
Officeholders, telephone numbers and changing administrative details are excluded from stable learner statements. No source attribution is a legal or clinical signoff.
